overview.title: Overview
overview.lead: You do not read first. The teacher asks, you predict, you try it in a simulation, and only then come theory and practice with evidence.

challenge.title: Asked
challenge.lead: This is an entry diagnostic and does not count toward passing. You will be asked this question again in the last phase to see how far you have come.

predict.title: Predict
predict.lead: Pick one answer. The explanation of each option appears only after you choose.

explore.title: Experiment
explore.lead: Take each action, read what you observe, then answer the debrief question.

explain.title: Understand
explain.lead: Read each theory section; each one ties back to what you observed in the earlier phases.

apply.title: Apply
apply.lead: Read the code of the model, then solve a new situation and submit your evidence.

reflect.title: Interview again
reflect.lead: Same rubric as the Asked phase. The teacher compares each criterion before and after. A longer answer earns no extra points.

review.title: Review
review.lead: Review questions come due 1, 7 and 21 days later and are graded by their own rubric.

pitch.title: Projects
pitch.description: Bring your own repo, prove each Essentials concept with evidence a machine can check, and get a verified CV line. Projects come with Premium.
pitch.stepsTitle: From your repo to a CV line

repo.title: Bring your own repo
repo.text: There is no sample project: every project is your own code, on any topic, in any language. One command adds a starci/ folder and a CI template to the repo.

prove.title: Prove each concept
prove.text: Every Essentials concept needs its evidence slots: a test, an e2e flow, a probe of your deployed address, or an AI read of the code you paste. Running on your machine is Practising; a CI run GitHub signs with OIDC, or a server re-run, is Proved.

queue.aiLine: CV line drafted by the AI
queue.noteLabel: Note for the learner (required to return)
queue.notePlaceholder: For example: the line says 'high load' but the probe only sent 50 requests; reword it or add evidence.
queue.rules: Three working days to review. A reviewer never reviews their own item. Every decision keeps the signer, the role and the time; the teacher can revoke later.
queue.approved: Verified. This item now reaches the learner's profile and CV.
queue.returned: Returned with a note. The learner edits it and sends it again.

refusal.CAREER_REVIEW_FORBIDDEN: You may not review this item.
refusal.CAREER_REVIEW_CONFLICT: Someone else just decided this item; the list was reloaded.
refusal.CAREER_NOT_VERIFIED: Only a verified item can be revoked.
refusal.other: The decision could not be saved; try again.
refusal.CAREER_REVIEWER_NOT_FOUND: No active reviewer has this id.
refusal.CAREER_STATE_CONFLICT: This item just changed state; reload it.
refusal.CAREER_SELF_REVIEW: Nobody may review their own item.

queue.reviewerSubjectHint: The Keycloak subject of an account that holds the Reviewer role.
queue.assignHint: A reviewer only takes items of the parts they are appointed to.

verify.revokedSub: StarCi revoked it on {date}. This CV line is no longer confirmed.
verify.notFoundDescription: This code matches no experience StarCi verified.
verify.note: This page lets a recruiter check one CV line. It shows no detailed score and no source code.

profile.title: Your profile
profile.description: Every item below was graded by StarCi, never self-reported.
profile.publicNote: The public profile and the CV show only verified items; the others are visible to you alone.
profile.gate: {count}/{min} verified items for a job introduction
profile.cvLater: CV export from verified items comes in a later round.

devices.codeHint: Only confirm a code you just ran yourself. Check the device name and system before you confirm.
devices.confirmed: {name} is connected. Your terminal will say so.
devices.devicesLimit: Premium: up to 2 devices. Free plan: 1 device.
devices.pageSub: Run code lessons on your own machine, results come back here
devices.emptyText: Do three steps and the machine shows here; you can revoke it any time.
devices.practiceText: Results run on your machine through the CLI. They help you practise and do not count towards a milestone.
devices.proofText: Signed CI or a server rerun.

step.installNote: Or run it with npx. The client source is public and releases are signed.
step.loginNote: The terminal prints an 8-character code and a link to this page.
step.confirmNote: Once confirmed, the device shows under Your devices and can be revoked at any time.

rule.manifest: Runs only the commands of the task manifest StarCi signed
rule.ask: Shows each command and asks you before it runs
rule.results: Sends test results, logs and the diffs you choose
rule.noSecrets: Never sends the whole repo, .env files or secret keys
rule.noShell: Never opens a remote shell and never edits your files

error.codeNotFound: The code is wrong or has expired. Run starci-next login again.
error.deviceLimit: You have connected as many devices as your plan allows. Revoke one and try again.
error.other: That did not go through; please try again.

connectAi.pageSub: Study with your own AI: it reads the lesson and the source, sees your run results and asks your machine to re-run a scenario.
connectAi.endpointHint: Paste this address into Claude or ChatGPT, then create an access token below so the AI signs in as you.
connectAi.tokensEmpty: You have no token yet. Name one (for example Claude) and press Create token.
connectAi.tokensLimit: You can hold up to 5 tokens at once. Revoking a token stops it at once.
connectAi.tokensError: The tokens could not be loaded.
connectAi.createdTitle: New token. Copy it now, it is shown only once.
connectAi.createdHint: Whoever holds this token can read your lessons and run results, so share it with no one. If you lose it, revoke it and create another.
connectAi.canTitle: What the AI can read and do
connectAi.canText: Read the unlocked parts of a lesson, read and search the source at the lesson's pinned commit, see the scenarios, your own run results and the laws you have opened. Ask your machine to re-run one scenario: the command shows on your machine and runs only when you confirm. Source, scenarios and re-runs need Premium like the lesson workspace.
connectAi.cannotText: Hidden tests, sample submissions, rubric answers, expected evidence and the faults injected in incidents. Letting the AI help fix your own code is fine; Proved still comes only from CI with GitHub OIDC.
connectAi.oauthNote: For now you connect with a personal access token (Bearer), which works at once with Claude Code and apps that let you add a header. OAuth sign-in for Claude web and ChatGPT comes in a later step.

error.limit: You already created 5 tokens. Revoke one and try again.
error.name: The token name is not valid (1 to 60 characters).
error.other: That did not work. Please try again later.

open.title: Open Connectors
open.note: In Claude: Settings, Connectors, Add custom connector.

add.title: Paste the MCP address
add.note: Name it StarCi Next and paste the address above. Claude web needs OAuth sign-in, which comes in a later step; meanwhile use Claude Code below.

code.title: Or add it to Claude Code
code.command: claude mcp add --transport http starci-next {endpoint} --header "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN"
code.note: Replace YOUR_TOKEN with the token you just created. Then type /mcp to check, and ask it to use the fix_scenario prompt for your lesson.

enable.title: Turn on developer mode
enable.note: In ChatGPT: Settings, Connectors (or Apps), Advanced, turn on Developer mode. Menu names can change between versions.

add.title: Create a connector from the MCP address
add.note: Choose Create, paste the address above and pick the sign-in method ChatGPT allows. OAuth sign-in comes in a later step.

use.title: Use it in a chat
use.note: Start a new chat, switch on the StarCi Next connector and name the lesson you study, for example: explain why the double-spend scenario is red on my machine.
